title: District Level Carbon Baseline Analysis and Pathways to Net Zero - AWARD
description:
West Oxfordshire District Council and Cherwell District Council are district local authorities. Both authorities have dedicated climate change teams who work collaboratively on net zero projects. 
      
      Both authorities have contributed to and endorsed the Oxfordshire Net Zero Route Map and Action Plan. This report presents a 'leading the way' pathway to net zero and identifies workstreams for Oxfordshire local authorities to develop collaboratively to provide a catalyst for positive action across the region. District-specific targets are noted, Cherwell references 2030 and West Oxfordshire 2050; however, the route map modelling focuses on an Oxfordshire-wide net zero by 2050. The Future Oxfordshire Strategic Vision aims for countywide net zero to be achieved by 2040.

title: Request for Quotation for Oxfordshire Gypsy and Traveller Accommodation Assessment and Boat Dweller Accommodation Assessment - AWARD
description:
Until August 2022, the five Local Planning Authorities in Oxfordshire were working together on a joint statutory development plan for the county to 2050 known as the 'Oxfordshire Plan 2050'. That work programme has now ended and, instead, individual Local Plans for the City and Districts will provide the framework for long term planning in Oxfordshire. 
      In the absence of the Oxfordshire Plan, the Oxfordshire Councils have agreed to continue to cooperate with each other as they prepare their own Local Plans including the joint commissioning of evidence where appropriate. 
      A study on the future accommodation needs of Gypsies, Travellers, Travelling Showpeople and Boat Dwellers has been identified as one such joint commission.

title: Town Centre Strategy and Needs Assessment - AWARD
description:
Officers are now targeting further Regulation 18 consultation in October 2024. The consultation will take the form of a 'preferred options' paper setting out the Council's preferred thinking on a range of policy topics including the quantum and distribution of future growth in the period up to 2041.
      The consultation feedback received will then help to inform the development of the pre-submission draft Regulation 19 version of the plan in spring 2025. 
      In accordance with national policy, a key function of the new Local Plan will be to support the role of West Oxfordshire's Town Centres by taking a positive approach towards their growth, management and adaptation. 
      There are a number of ways this can be done and to inform its preferred approach, the Council is seeking to commission a new Town Centre Strategy and Needs Assessment

      Rats
      Bird mites
      Flies
      Mice
      Lice
      Dust Mites
      Cockroaches
      Fleas
      Ants
      Bed Bugs
      Wasps
      Silverfish
      Squirrels

      The only exceptions are protected species & honeybees (where Midland Heart will decide on how to proceed following advice from the Contractor).
      
      The services will be delivered direct through the Contractors own staff and will not be subcontracted without written permission from Midland Heart.
